Summary (high level):
- Hosted API: target RTO for a regional outage (automated routing + model fallback) is 60 seconds for control-plane failover; end-to-end tail latency recovery depends on model spin-up and caching (typical recovery to steady state ~5–10 minutes).
- Dedicated (reserved) capacity: we provide configurable warm-standby pools. For dedicated tenants who opt into cross-zone replication, typical RTO to restore throughput is 2–5 minutes once compute is available.
- RPO: customer data persistence for request/response logs and audit trails is asynchronous to a central ledger; RPO is typically under 60 seconds for stateful control-plane metadata. For model KV cache and in-flight session data, we recommend session affinity and a short RPO expectation (ephemeral cache is best-effort).
- Mode recommendation: Bronze (single-region) — documented SLA with scheduled DR rehearsals; Silver — warm-standby cross-zone replication; Gold — multi-region active-routing.

Actions:
1) Aditya will provide the failover sequencing and specific RTO/RPO numbers per mode (attached runbook excerpt).
2) We'll share SOC 2 / attestations link and a sanitized runbook excerpt we can include in procurement materials.
3) Offer to run a tabletop drill and share rehearsal notes if that helps the committee.

Sienna / team —

Quick technical addendum with sequencing, assumptions and numbers. I'm pasting the runbook excerpt below and attaching the diagram referenced by Vanessa. If you'd like, we can redact any customer-identifying pieces for procurement.

Assumptions:
- Models are pre-warmed in snapshot images and can be instantiated on compatible instance types within 90–120s per worker for cold starts; continuous-batching and KV cache optimizations reduce steady-state spin-up time for many workloads.
- Customer data flows (logs, request metadata) replicate asynchronously to an immutable ledger in a separate region; log replication lag target <60s under normal load.

Failover sequencing (simplified):
1) Detection: regional health probes + control-plane anomaly detection raise an incident. Automated routing policy evaluates latency & capacity and triggers policy execution.
2) Automated fallback: requests for compatible model variants are routed to next-best region/tier (platform-level routing switch within 60s). For dedicated customers with cross-zone replication configured, routing pins to warm-standby pool.
3) Capacity ramp: orchestration boots reserved or burst-capable GPUs in target region; model containers restore KV cache from persisted snapshots where available. Recommended warm-standby config keeps minimal pre-warmed workers to meet baseline throughput.
4) Traffic reflow: once backpressure is acceptable, traffic is progressively returned to normal regions; we prefer incremental reweighting to avoid cascading cold-starts.
5) Failback: after root cause remediation, we execute an orderly failback with state reconciliation windows and can coordinate a maintenance window with the customer.

Target RTO / RPO by product mode (typical):
- Hosted API (standard): RTO (automated routing + degraded capacity) = 60s for control-plane switch; full throughput recovery (steady state) 5–10 minutes; RPO for control-plane metadata & logs <60s.
- Dedicated (reserved): RTO (warm-standby enabled) = 2–5 minutes to restore throughput to committed levels; if warm-standby not enabled, boot times dominate (5–12 minutes). RPO for committed tenant metadata <60s.
- Private (on-prem / VPC): RTO depends on customer infra; our orchestrator supports scripted failover sequences and we provide runbook templates. Typical guidance: aim for <15 minutes if pre-provisioned.

Data consistency notes:
- Model KV caches are treated as ephemeral caches; we persist model state snapshots periodically but not every in-flight token. Session reconstruction requires application-level sticky sessions or short-lived session replay tooling.

Test evidence included:
- redwood_continuity_evidence_v2.pdf — rehearsal logs and play-by-play from a recent regional failover test (anonymized).
- diagram_multi_zone_failover.png — sequence diagram for routing and capacity ramp.

Open items:
- We can provide a sanitized runbook excerpt and an ops run-deck (.md) for the procurement file.
- If you require SLA language edits for RTO guarantees, we'll need to align on tier selection and reserved capacity commitments.

- Aditya (Principal SRE, Redwood Inference)
